solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Efficient by virtue of assuming nothing

indicators.note: to assume is to take on or put on, so the phrase for 'by virtue of' takes the zero into itself

parts.note: 'through' can mean by means of, as in 'through hard work'
O, the round zero for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone doing a job well because they take nothing for granted.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough worker is careful and complete, which is to say efficient in a painstaking way.

clue.text: Programme with very wearing new host going ahead

indicators.note: what is wearing clothes is inside them, so the letter for very sits inside the rearranged letters
new signals the letters of host in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A broadcast in which the host, sporting something novel, takes the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns HOST into TSHO, and 'wearing' sets V inside it to give TVSHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A television broadcast is a programme on the box.

clue.text: Start up hotel by river where everyone's welcome, any time

parts.note: to start up a business is to open it
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Setting up a riverside hotel that welcomes all comers round the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several rivers in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping open house means offering hospitality to all visitors at all times.

clue.text: Quiet in class!

definitions.meaning: '...!' is the call for quiet, as from a chairman or Speaker

explanation.surface: A teacher calling for silence in the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry for silence in a meeting, and a taxonomic rank between class and family, share this word.

clue.text: Fine times echo for so long

parts.note: fine means good
'by' is the multiplication sign read aloud, as in two by three
E is echo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pleasant times echoing on for a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: 'So long' is an informal farewell, the same parting word.

clue.text: Rock and roll band leaders with macho clothing

indicators.note: clothing wraps round a body, so the word for macho is wrapped round the two leading letters

parts.note: macho means manly, so male

indicators.note: leaders are the front runners, so take the first letters of roll and band

explanation.surface: A rock-and-roll group fronted by men in macho outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock and roll' reads as one music phrase, but 'Rock' is the definition and 'and' just links it.
explanation.definitionFit: Marble is a metamorphic stone, so it is a kind of rock.

clue.text: Moderate a tale about tackling vile criminal

indicators.note: to tackle is to take hold of, so the shuffled tale grips the shuffled vile
about means around in a new arrangement, so the letters of tale are rearranged
criminal means bent or crooked, so vile's letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A story about someone taking on a wicked lawbreaker, toned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'criminal' look like the story's subject matter, but both stir letters: TALE becomes LATE and VILE becomes LEVI, which 'tackling' grips.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate pain is to lessen or ease it, making it milder.

clue.text: Instrument's seize-up curtailed task

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to nab is to seize

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a job is a task

explanation.surface: A seizure that cut a job short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seize-up' looks like one word, a breakdown, but splits into the synonym and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The banjo is a stringed musical instrument with a drum-like body.

clue.text: Next real trip is not in this country

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters of next real stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: The next genuine journey will be abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' reads as a journey, fitting the surface, but signals the letters falling over.
explanation.definitionFit: External affairs are foreign affairs, those concerning other nations rather than home.

clue.text: Just a Minute's still broadcasting

parts.note: still in the sense of motionless, steady
a programme being broadcast is on air, ON

explanation.surface: The long-running radio panel game Just a Minute is still being broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Just a Minute is a BBC radio panel show, which hides the exclamation 'just a minute!' used to urge caution.
explanation.definitionFit: Both exclamations urge someone to pause and calm down before going further, so they are interchangeable.

clue.text: Mars perhaps has energy feeding living organism

indicators.note: food goes into an organism, so the energy symbol is put inside the word for living thing

parts.note: a plant is a living organism
E, the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A Mars chocolate bar gives energy to whoever eats it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mars' looks like the chocolate bar, but here it is the planet; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is the fourth body orbiting the Sun, an example of a world in our solar system.

clue.text: Last to try travelling north to see bird

indicators.note: names the letter that moves: the last one in the word for try
in a down clue, travelling north means going up to the top

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it

explanation.surface: A final attempt to head north to spot a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last to' and 'travelling north' together move the R of HEAR from the bottom of the down entry to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Worry boy's ignored, being different

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so the letter for boy is dropped

parts.note: to worry is to bother
B, the standard abbreviation for boy (as in births columns)

explanation.surface: A worried boy being overlooked because he is not like the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means not the same as the one already mentioned, so it is a synonym of distinct or unlike.

clue.text: Conduct live audio-visual interviews, initially filling time

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so these letters go inside the word for time

parts.note: an hour is a period of time

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of interviews

explanation.surface: Instructions to run live audio-visual interviews, with the opening ones taking up the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conduct' looks like a verb here (to conduct interviews), but it is the noun for how one behaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's conduct is the way they act, which is their behaviour.

clue.text: Queen ordered nice fruit

indicators.note: ordered means arranged into a new order, so the letters of nice are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Queen requested a pleasant piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a hard, pear-shaped yellow fruit used for jelly and preserves.

clue.text: Spy novels put at the front in WH Smith perhaps

indicators.note: says the news comes before the spy

parts.note: novel things are new things, so novels are news
a spy is an agent

explanation.surface: Spy thrillers displayed prominently in a WH Smith shop.
explanation.walkthrough: WH Smith is a British high-street chain selling newspapers, magazines and books.
explanation.definitionFit: WH Smith sells newspapers and magazines, so it is an example of a shop of that kind.

clue.text: American former President's heading off, crossing Louisiana state

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it, so these letters lie across the state's abbreviation
with its heading, or first letter, taken off

parts.note: Barack Obama, former US President
LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana

explanation.surface: A former US President beheads his way across Louisiana into another state.
explanation.walkthrough: The former President is Barack Obama; 'crossing' means the American pieces stretch across both sides of the Louisiana abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty United States, in the Deep South.

clue.text: When nursing bad back competently, everything's OK

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the word for when holds the reversed word for bad

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: back means the word for bad runs backwards

parts.note: bad means ill
done competently is done well

explanation.surface: Once a bad back has been nursed properly, all is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: 'All is well' says that nothing is wrong, the same reassurance.

clue.text: Drunk lad, losing leader, lied and improvised

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady, so the letters of lad lurch out of order
losing its leader, its first letter goes

parts.note: to fib is to lie, so lied is fibbed

explanation.surface: A drunk young man, falling behind, told lies and made things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing leader' looks like it goes with 'lad', but it trims the synonym for 'lied'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad-lib is to speak without preparation, making it up on the spot.

clue.text: Idea to reform system in decline

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters of idea are formed into a new order

parts.note: a way of doing things is a system or method

explanation.surface: A proposal to overhaul a system that is going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: To die away is to fade gradually, as a sound does, so it means to dwindle or decline.

clue.text: Jerk's always turning up heartily zonked

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: ay is an old word for always

indicators.note: heartily means from the heart, the middle letters of zonked

explanation.surface: A twit who always shows up utterly exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like the insult but is the verb for a sharp pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a sudden sharp pull is to tug or wrench it.

clue.text: Mothers' Union takes on lies concocted for healthy breakfast cereal

parts.note: MU is the abbreviation for the Mothers' Union, a Christian charity

indicators.note: concocted means made up or mixed, so the letters of lies are mixed

explanation.surface: The Mothers' Union tackles invented stories about a wholesome breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mothers' Union is an Anglican women's charity in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten at breakfast, seen as a wholesome option.

clue.text: Person who delivers morning's first papers with mate

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of morning

parts.note: ID, identity papers
a wife is a mate or spouse

explanation.surface: A paper boy bringing the morning newspapers with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person who delivers' suggests a paper round, but it is babies that are delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: A midwife assists at childbirth, helping to bring babies into the world.

clue.text: Runs away taking member's computer stuff

parts.note: a leg is a member or limb, and with the 's it gives legs
IT, information technology

explanation.surface: Someone flees with a colleague's computer equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg it' is British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: To leg it is slang for running off fast, so this is the third-person form, fleeing.

clue.text: Fixed gin cocktail and threw it down

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed

parts.note: 'throw it down' is a colloquial phrase for heavy rain

explanation.surface: Someone made a gin cocktail and gulped it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Threw it down' reads as drinking fast, but means it poured with rain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrained habit is firmly embedded and hard to shift, that is, fixed.

clue.text: Sharp intake of breath over king's command

indicators.note: the gasp is placed over the king, covering him so that he ends up inside it

parts.note: a gasp is a sharp intake of breath
R, for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A shocked gasp at a royal decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'command' looks like an order, but means mastery, as in a good command of French.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm grasp of a subject is a mastery or command of it.

clue.text: Test sample of barista's tea

indicators.note: sample of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Try a sip of the tea the coffee-shop server has made.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food or drink is to try or sample it, a way of testing it.

clue.text: Complete non-drinker's getting in round with alcohol content removed

indicators.note: the round gets into the abstainer's letters

parts.note: TT, teetotal, a non-drinker
O is round in shape

indicators.note: with its contents taken out, only the outer letters of alcohol are left

explanation.surface: A teetotaller buys a round of drinks with the alcohol taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in round' reads as buying drinks, but puts O inside TT.
explanation.definitionFit: Total and complete both mean entire or absolute, as in a total stranger.

clue.text: Unabashed, zebra strays close to lion

indicators.note: to stray is to wander off, so the letters of zebra wander out of order
the close of a word is its end, so take the last letter of lion

explanation.surface: A bold zebra wanders right up near a lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazen describes shameless boldness, someone not embarrassed at all.

clue.text: Bandage is not ultimately stopping pain

indicators.note: a stopping fills a gap, so these letters plug the inside of the word for bandage

parts.note: to bandage a wound is to dress it

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of not

explanation.surface: A bandage that does not, in the end, stop the hurting.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is acute suffering, whether mental or physical, so it means anguish or pain.

clue.text: Second-in-command takes responsibility, keeping record

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the record is held inside

parts.note: a duty is a responsibility
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A number two shoulders the burden while keeping the minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is the person ranked just below a leader who stands in for them.

clue.text: Pitched apartment failed to impress

parts.note: to pitch forward is to fall, so pitched gives fell
a flat is an apartment

explanation.surface: A sales pitch for a flat that left buyers cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke or performance that falls flat gets no response, an idiom for flopping.
